issues.claim: Missed shared subject: item 124's weather effects layer over V04's underground view has no stated outcome. §8.8 *The weather effects layer* (l. 14097–14109) draws the spell every frame 'above the tiles and below the labels, the chrome and every overlay'; §8.4 (i) (l. 13599–13617) adds per-frame terms beyond the direct-light multiplier — fog and mist fading the picture toward `fog` from the view's centre, at night a soft halo on 'every drawn LightSource (§8.1 item 7)', heat shimmer offsetting 'the base's sampling', dust fading toward `sand`; §8.2 *Weather effects* gives the falling marks and ripples. None names a layer. V04 §5.1 draws the underground, when visible, as `cutaway` (ground ghosted), `overlay` or `solo` ('the underground alone', the export default), and §8.4 (e) says 'Underground there is no global light at any setting'. So with Below shown it is undefined whether rain and snow fall over a sewer's plan, fog fades the band and haloes the undercity's torches, or shimmer moves the rock. No test sweeps it: T-ER-29 (§8.11) names no layer, V12 §3.15.14's edge row 35 lists no layer, V04 §3.11 and §5.1 are silent. Principle (11): every layer on and off has a defined outcome and test; the effects layer is rendering's (canon routing of item 124).
issues.required_change: §8.8 *The weather effects layer* adds: 'While the underground layer is drawn (V04 §5.1's `cutaway`, `overlay` or `solo`), the spell draws nothing over the view — no mark, ripple, fog, mist or dust fade, shimmer or night halo — and §8.4 (i)'s terms are not applied (the underground has no global light, §8.4 (e)); the effects return when the underground layer is hidden, the spell's timeline running on (§6.1's `view.weather`).' §8.4 (i) states the same in one clause; T-ER-29 adds 'the underground layer drawn in each of its three modes during a spell' with 'nothing drawn, the underground tiles and light byte-identical with the effects on and off'; V04 §5.1 cites §8.8's rule in one clause (V04's end, R2-05).

issues.claim: `depthBand` crosses the bridge under round 2's §11.3, against the units that make it per viewer. Before round 2, §11.3's *View state* sent every view key across but the pointer and `underlay`; VRC1T-02 (R2-33 (b)) rewrote it (l. 16277–16281) to name 'the per-viewer keys a viewer's client keeps — `yearWeek`, `seasonFollow`, `festival`, `cvdVariant`, `find` and `crises` (§2.9), `thematic`, `workingLayer`, `showUnexcavated` and V09 §4.19's per-viewer keys —, which never cross the bridge'. The list leaves out `depthBand`, the underground's drawn band, which §8.4 (l. 13368) calls 'the per-viewer view key `depthBand` (§2.9)', V04 §1b.3 (l. 373) groups with `showUnexcavated` as set 'by V09's per-viewer controls', and V09's `WorkingLayer` (V09 l. 518) keeps as the band of the per-viewer working layer ('the view key `depthBand` alone (§2.9), never copied here'); V09 §4.19's table, to which §11.3 delegates, does not carry it, and §2.9's entry (l. 3293) does not mark it per viewer. Read by §11.3 — the key's home for what travels (R2-33 (b)) — a host's or another viewer's band change moves this viewer's drawn band and Find's Go there target while that viewer's working layer stays: the two readings sync the view differently.
issues.required_change: §11.3's never-cross list adds `depthBand` beside `workingLayer` and `showUnexcavated`: '… `thematic`, `workingLayer`, `depthBand` (the underground's drawn band, V04 §5.1), `showUnexcavated` and V09 §4.19's per-viewer keys —, which never cross the bridge'. §2.9's entry needs no change (it defers which keys travel to §11.3).

issues.claim: §6.3 *Plan damage* (l. 9786–9792), the home of the threshold's key, lists 'the id's parts — its element kind and V03 §2.2's plan-part id (`wall:`, `op:`, `win:`, `core:`, `furn:`), a floor area and the roof bay over a room by their room's address'. It has no form for V04 §5.6 (2)'s room-keyed kinds below ground (l. 2887–2889): `cellarVault` keyed by 'the room's id' and `cryptVault` by '(its room's id, the cell's grid node (i, j)) … a key, never a new id', each cell with its own threshold ('a rubble heap filling the cell, its columns standing'). Read as exhaustive, §6.3 folds every `cryptVault` cell of a crypt to one key (kind and room address), so every bay falls at one level, against V04's per-cell thresholds and T-V4-82 (c). VV34-r2-03 raises the other half (which node names a cell).
issues.required_change: §6.3's sentence reads: '… a floor area, the roof bay over a room and a `cellarVault` by their room's address, and a `cryptVault` cell by its room's address and the cell's grid node (V04 §5.6 (2)) — folded into the key …'. ONE FIX with VV34-r2-03, whose V04 end fixes the node that names the cell.

issues.claim: Same defect as VV78-r2-05 (vol-V07-V08), a rung rule shared by this lane's members. V07 §1 (15) (l. 197–200) hands §10.2 'its places read at the village rungs as V07 §5.6 (2) states'. §10.2 *Crisis looks*, the placement home, does not carry that end: (d) defines the main approach road by §4.3's `TradeFlow` and `affectedQuarter` as 'the district …', and only `neighbourhoods` cites V07; (f) draws `siege`'s 'line of trenches and earthworks round the walled arcs' at every rung with walled arcs, which §8.2's siege row (l. 12892) draws. V07 §5.6 (1) (l. 3400–3402) and T-V7-69 draw no siege line at THORP or HAMLET — item 122 (c)'s 'a hamlet gets a war band's camp, a city a full siege line', which §13.2's T122-5 (l. 18159) also quotes — and no V11 `scale` cell can suppress the line (they are camped-ground areas). The base and V07 draw a hamlet's siege differently.
issues.required_change: ONE FIX with VV78-r2-05, in its words: §10.2 (c) adds that a share s of a place's n units takes round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s > 0 and none where s ≤ 0 (V01 §3.16 (5)'s count); (d) adds 'at THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE the main approach road, the outskirts' land and each place below read on the village's records as V07 §5.6 (2) states, `affectedQuarter` a unit of V07 §5.6 (3)'; (f)'s `siege` reads 'at VILLAGE and above, a line of trenches and earthworks round the walled arcs at it — none at THORP and HAMLET, item 122 (c)'s war band's camp (V07 §5.6 (1))'; (h) adds 'and no siege line at THORP and HAMLET'. §8.2's siege row draws the line where §10.2 places it and needs no change.
